items.reasoning: The table has only three data points (1617, 1700, 1750), so C's 'rising every single year without fail' cannot be shown from it. D contradicts the table (tobacco was nearly three-fourths of Chesapeake exports in 1750). B is unsupported and wrong. A is the only option that challenges 'quick riches alone' — growth depended on imported labor and new land, not just planter desire.

The passage says the difference was 'not the climate — New England was colder — but what the settlers came to do and how they organized themselves.' C restates that directly. A contradicts the passage, B is false (neither colony failed and restarted), D blames poor soil, which the passage never says.

Williams criticizes civil power imposing a religion — the Puritan establishment of Massachusetts Bay, in New England. The middle colonies (C) were the tolerant ones, not the ones imposing a state church; the Chesapeake (D) and southern colonies (A) are not the group Williams broke with.

The passage says Williams founded Providence welcoming every faith, Hutchinson carried followers to Rhode Island, Hooker founded Hartford with government chosen by the people — each left Massachusetts and founded a freer colony. B is false (none returned to England), C is false (Hutchinson was not a minister, and none 'became Puritan ministers' after leaving), D is false (three different colonies).

The passage's final sentence is the key: 'each new colony was a little freer than the one it left.' C restates it. A contradicts (colonies were not destroyed), B contradicts (dissent had a lasting effect), D contradicts (Massachusetts did not become tolerant).

Franklin fears Pennsylvania will be 'Germanized' — Germans 'shortly be so numerous' — so the German population had grown large enough to worry English founders. A contradicts the quote, C contradicts it (no ban), D contradicts it (Germans had not adopted English language/customs).

The prospect shows a grid city of brick houses, churches and public buildings, with sailing ships crowding the river loading and unloading at the wharves — a commercial center built on trade and town life. A is wrong (Pennsylvania was diverse), B is wrong (not tobacco — that is the Chesapeake), C is wrong (religious diversity existed).

The passage lists fishing, shipbuilding, carrying, cattle, timber, grain and livestock — 'a patchwork, not a plantation' — directly against the Chesapeake's one-crop economy. A is false (different economies), C is false (New England did not grow tobacco), D is false (the passage describes trade with other colonies).

Selling grain and livestock to the sugar islands is one leg of intercolonial trade — each colony selling what the others needed. A contradicts the passage (New England carried goods for other colonies), B reverses the flow (New England sold TO the islands), D contradicts it (trade partners, not rivals).
